summary: Urmia Airport (OMH/OITR) is a medium-sized domestic airport serving the city of Urmia, the capital of Iran's West Azerbaijan Province in the country's mountainous northwest. Situated near the shores of the iconic Lake Urmia—one of the largest salt lakes in the world—the airport primarily handles flights connecting the region to Tehran and other major Iranian cities. It serves as a key gateway for travelers visiting the culturally distinct Azerbaijani region of Iran.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Urmia Airport?
A: The IATA code is OMH and the ICAO code is OITR.

Q: Does Urmia Airport offer international flights?
A: The airport primarily operates domestic flights within Iran, with international service being very limited or seasonal.

Q: How far is Urmia Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 10-15 km (6-9 miles) north of downtown Urmia, with typical taxi rides taking around 20-30 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: When is the best time to visit Urmia for travel through this airport?
A: Spring (April to June) and early autumn (September to October) offer the most pleasant weather for visiting the Urmia region and Lake Urmia area.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most common and reliable way to reach Urmia Airport, with both shared and private options typically available outside the terminal. Travelers should arrange return transportation in advance, as ride-sharing apps may not operate in the region. The airport's location near the main highway connecting Urmia to Tabriz makes it a convenient departure point for overland connections as well.
